original_text: TOKYO, Japan (Reuters) -- A Japanese bullet train carrying about 130 passengers and crew derailed in northern Japan on Saturday after being hit by a strong earthquake, but there were no injuries, police and news reports said. The Shinkansen train was traveling near the city of Nagaoka, about 250 km (160 miles) north of Tokyo, when the quake with a preliminary magnitude of 6.8 struck the area. The tremor, which was centered in Niigata prefecture, was strong enough to sway buildings in Tokyo. Several carriages of the train came off the rails, a police spokesman said. Public broadcaster NHK quoted the train's driver as saying: "I felt a tremor and the train shook. I applied the emergency brake but the train didn't stop right away." It was the first time a Japanese bullet train had derailed since the high-speed network went into service in 1964.
